title: Establish file ownership classes; verify bd's rewrite behaviour
description:
Why: provenance check (2026-08-31) disproves the premise of the previous reconciliation plan.

EVIDENCE:
- git log --follow: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md were both created by a single commit, 4d81b55 'bd init: initialize beads issue tracking', alongside 16 other files (.agents/, .claude/, .codex/, .beads/).
- Both are byte-identical to that commit today. Neither has ever been hand-edited. Zero human-authored lines.
- 'bd setup --list' shows 13 built-in recipes; these files are recipe OUTPUT.
- 'bd setup claude --check' reports CLAUDE.md as 'installed but stale' and instructs 'Run: bd setup claude'. bd actively claims ownership and considers the file out of date right now.
- 'bd setup codex --check' reports AGENTS.md, .codex/hooks.json and .agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md as installed and current.

CONSEQUENCE: the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md difference is not policy drift. It is bd template-version skew between two recipe installs (block hash 6cd5cc61 stale vs 970c3bf2 current). Nobody ever decided the 'bd dolt push' line; a template did. Extracting these files into canonical/policy would have forked vendor boilerplate into our source of truth, where it would rot against future bd versions and be overwritten by the next bd setup.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW DOES:
1. Record three ownership classes in SUBSTRATE.md terms:
   CANONICAL  - authored by us. Today: README.md, BASELINE.md. Policy content: currently NONE.
   VENDOR     - owned by another tool's installer; regenerated by it; verifiable via its own check command. Today: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/settings.json, .codex/*, .agents/skills/beads/*.
   PROJECTED  - derived by bin/ms from canonical.
2. EXPERIMENT, in a throwaway copy of this repo, never the live tree: add sentinel content to CLAUDE.md both INSIDE and OUTSIDE the BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION markers, run 'bd setup claude', and record precisely what bd preserves and what it replaces.
3. From that result, determine the composition seam: whether our policy can coexist in a vendor file (out-of-marker region survives) or must live in a separate file the harness composes.

Do not run 'bd setup claude' in the live repo. Do not write canonical policy fragments in this bead.
design:
OWNERSHIP TABLE — every path present in the repo, one class each (verified 2026-08-31 via git ls-files, git log, and bd setup --check).

CANONICAL (authored by us; the substrate's source of truth)
  README.md                        commit 479ee18 'Initialize machine-state'
  BASELINE.md                      commit 4e74e46, hand-written inventory
  Policy content: NONE EXISTS YET. No human has authored a line of agent policy in this repo.

VENDOR (owned by bd's installers; regenerated by them; verify with bd setup <recipe> --check)
  CLAUDE.md                        recipe: claude   marker-delimited block + template stubs
  AGENTS.md                        recipe: codex    TWO marker blocks (INTEGRATION + CODEX SETUP)
  .claude/settings.json            recipe: claude   SessionStart hook, whole-file JSON
  .codex/config.toml               recipe: codex
  .codex/hooks.json                recipe: codex
  .agents/skills/beads/**          recipe: codex    bd owns the beads/ subdir, NOT the skills/ parent
  .beads/**                        bd's own data dir, incl. tracked config.yaml, metadata.json,
                                   hooks/*, README.md, .gitignore, and generated issues.jsonl
  .gitignore                       written by bd init; SPECIAL CASE, see below

PROJECTED (derived by bin/ms from canonical)
  Nothing yet.

SPECIAL CASE — .gitignore: vendor-authored but carries NO marker pair, only a comment header
('# Beads / Dolt files (added by bd init)'). It is co-owned by convention rather than protocol.
bd writes it at init, not on every setup, so the practical risk is low, but the substrate must
append its own commented section and must never rewrite the file whole.

SPECIAL CASE — .beads/issues.jsonl: untracked, NOT gitignored, and regenerated automatically
(export.auto: true in config.yaml). Vendor-generated data that will keep reappearing in
git status. Classify VENDOR-GENERATED; the substrate must not manage it.

COMPOSITION SEAM — chosen, justified by the machine-state-9tw.2 experiment

  Claude   splice ./CLAUDE.md   marker 'MACHINE-STATE POLICY'
  Codex    splice ./AGENTS.md   marker 'MACHINE-STATE POLICY'

Both files are VENDOR-owned but splice-safe: the experiment proved bd replaces only its own
marker pair, leaves foreign blocks in the same file untouched, appends at EOF when its markers
are absent, and removes only its own block. Using the same marker name for both agents means
both harnesses receive identical canonical policy through an identical mechanism — which is
precisely the interchangeability the epic is trying to buy.

Rejected alternative: an @import line in the vendor file pointing at a wholly-projected
POLICY.md. The sentinel proved such a line survives every bd operation, but it depends on
harness import support that is unverified for Codex, and it leaves one unmanaged line in a file
we do not own. Splice needs no such support.

GOVERNING PRINCIPLE (generalised from the experiment)
  Own the smallest addressable region, never the container.
    - within a file: our marker pair, never the whole file
    - within a directory: our own subdirectory, never the shared parent
bd follows exactly this rule (it owns .agents/skills/beads/, not .agents/skills/), which is why
co-tenancy works at all. The substrate adopts it as law.

CONSEQUENCE for machine-state-9tw.4: the planned 'link ~/.claude/skills' target is WRONG — it
claims a container another installer may later populate. Link individual skill directories
(~/.claude/skills/<name>) instead. Note also that ~/.agents/skills/ is a potential vendor path,
since bd's codex recipe has a --global variant that installs ~/.agents/skills/beads/; sibling
skill subdirectories there remain safe.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ownership classes recorded, with every current repo path assigned to exactly one class.
- DONE: experiment run in throwaway copies; behaviour recorded verbatim in notes.
- DONE: live repo verified byte-identical to 4d81b55 after the experiment.
- Composition seam chosen for Claude and Codex and recorded in SUBSTRATE.md terms (recommendation: marker-delimited splice; see machine-state-9tw.3).
notes:
SUPERSEDED PROPOSAL (2026-08-31): an earlier plan in this bead proposed extracting these files into canonical/policy fragments (00-generated, 10-identity, 20-task-tracking, 30-authority, 40-session-close, 50-shell-hygiene, agents/*). Withdrawn — it treated vendor boilerplate as our policy. The disposition table it produced remains useful only as evidence that 100% of both files is bd-generated.

NOTED SEPARATELY: CLAUDE.md is stale per 'bd setup claude --check'. Refreshing it is a vendor-maintenance action, not substrate work. Do not fold it into this bead.

EXPERIMENT RESULT (2026-08-31, bd 1.2.2, throwaway copies under scratchpad/exp1 and exp2; live repo verified byte-identical to 4d81b55 before and after).

METHOD: planted sentinels inside and outside the managed markers, ran the real recipes, diffed.

CLAUDE.md / 'bd setup claude' — output: 'Updated existing beads section in CLAUDE.md'. Diff was exactly 3 lines, ALL inside the markers:
  - hash 6cd5cc61 -> 970c3bf2
  - in-block sentinel deleted
  - 'bd dolt push' line added
  SURVIVED: modified H1, line immediately above BEGIN, an @import-style line, line below END.
  REMOVED: only the in-block sentinel.
  This confirms the template-skew theory outright: after setup, CLAUDE.md is byte-equal to the AGENTS.md block. The 'bd dolt push' difference was never a decision.

AGENTS.md / 'bd setup codex' — diff was ONE line: the sentinel inside the CODEX SETUP block. The sentinel inside the BEADS INTEGRATION block in the same file SURVIVED, because that block belongs to a different recipe. Block ownership is PER-RECIPE, not per-file.

--remove: surgical. Removed only its own block and its SessionStart hook; every out-of-marker sentinel survived. Leaves .claude/settings.json as {"hooks":{}} rather than deleting it.

Re-install onto a MARKERLESS file: 'Added beads section to existing CLAUDE.md' — appended at the end, all pre-existing content preserved. bd never claims the whole file.

CONCLUSION: bd is a well-behaved co-tenant. It owns a marker-delimited region, appends if absent, replaces in place if present, removes cleanly, and ignores other owners' markers.

THEREFORE co-ownership of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md is SAFE, but only if our projector also confines itself to a region. A whole-file render would delete bd's block, bd would re-append it on next setup, and ms diff would flag it forever — a ping-pong loop.

INCIDENTAL BD BUG: 'bd setup <recipe> --check' ignores the global -C flag and inspects the real cwd (reports '✗ No hooks installed' for a correctly-installed copy). Any tooling that shells out to it must cd, not use -C.
close_reason: Ownership table complete (every repo path classified), bd rewrite behaviour verified experimentally, composition seam chosen: splice into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with marker 'MACHINE-STATE POLICY'. Live repo byte-identical to 4d81b55 throughout.

title: Author the minimal canonical policy fragments
description:
Why: machine-state-9tw.4 cannot write manifests with no sources to point at, and no bead ever created canonical policy content. The original reconciliation bead was withdrawn once machine-state-9tw.2 proved CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are 100 percent bd-generated, and nothing took its place. This is that gap.

SCOPE BOUNDARY, deliberate: this bead authors only SUBSTRATE-MECHANICAL content — facts about how this repo works and about each harness. It does NOT author substantive operating policy (how an agent should handle git, task tracking, shell hygiene). Two reasons: that is the user's call, not the substrate's; and bd already injects its own task-tracking guidance through a vendor-owned block plus the SessionStart hook, so duplicating it in our region would create exactly the two-copies-drifting problem this substrate exists to end.

Fragments:
  canonical/policy/00-generated.md      short banner: this region is generated, edit canonical and run ms project
  canonical/policy/10-substrate.md      what machine-state is; the canonical-to-projection rule; pointer to SUBSTRATE.md
  canonical/policy/agents/claude-harness.md   Claude-specific facts
  canonical/policy/agents/codex-harness.md    Codex-specific facts

Harness fragments carry only verified facts, not preferences:
  Claude - .claude/settings.json runs bd prime at SessionStart, so beads context arrives without asking; the harness ephemeral task tools are named TodoWrite and TaskCreate; neutral skills are linked into ~/.claude/skills.
  Codex  - no SessionStart injection here, so bd prime must be run explicitly; the beads skill lives at .agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md; Codex 0.129.0+ has native hooks, inspected with /hooks.
design: Keep our spliced region SHORT. It shares a file with bd's block, and a long region in someone else's file is bad manners and invites conflict. The region should say what only we can say: that the file is partly generated, where the truth lives, and how to change it.
acceptance_criteria:
- All four fragments exist and are referenced by the manifests in machine-state-9tw.4.
- Content is factual and verifiable; no invented preferences.
- No duplication of anything bd's own managed block already states.
- Combined spliced region stays well under one screen.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-08-31: four fragments, 29 lines total. Plus canonical/skills/machine-state/SKILL.md (40 lines), which was not in the original bead but is required — the link target in machine-state-9tw.4 needs a skill to point at, and 'own the smallest region' forbids linking the ~/.claude/skills container instead.

Held to the scope boundary: everything authored is either a fact about this repo or a verified fact about a harness. No operating preferences invented; none of bd's own guidance duplicated. Substantive policy is deferred to machine-state-sd8.
close_reason: Four mechanical policy fragments plus the machine-state skill authored; factual only, no duplication of bd's block.

title: Projector orphans targets removed from a manifest
description:
Found immediately after machine-state-9tw.3 closed, while verifying hash stability.

Remove a target from an adapters/*.toml and run ms project: the projected file stays on disk, its record stays in state/projection.json, and neither ms status nor ms diff mentions it. It becomes state nobody tracks. Retargeting an adapter therefore silently leaves the old projection behind, which undermines both the drift model and the promise in SUBSTRATE.md section 8 that the substrate can be cleanly removed.

Fix: treat a record whose key no target claims as an ORPHAN.
- ms project reconciles: removes the orphan and drops its record.
- ms status and ms diff report orphans rather than ignoring them.
- Removal must be conservative. A render orphan is deleted only if its bytes still match the recorded sha; if a human has since edited it, leave it in place and say so. splice orphans lose only our marker region. link orphans are just a symlink.

Reproduced 2026-08-31 in a scratch copy: dropped a link target from the manifest, projected, and linkdest remained on disk with its record intact and no command reporting it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Removing a target from a manifest and running ms project removes the projection and its record.
- ms status and ms diff name orphans explicitly.
- A render orphan whose content was edited after projection is NOT deleted; it is reported and left alone.
- unproject uses the same conservative removal path.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-31. Added orphans() plus a shared remove_recorded() used by both project reconciliation and unproject, so the two can never diverge in how carefully they remove things.

Conservative removal by kind: link unlinks a symlink; splice removes only our marker region; render deletes ONLY if the bytes still match the recorded sha, otherwise reports 'edited since we wrote it; left in place' and keeps the file.

VERIFIED: dropping a target from a manifest now shows as orphan in diff (exit 1) and status, and ms project removes it and clears the record. An edited render orphan survives both project and unproject. Full regression after the change: idempotent and hash-stable over three runs, diff clean exit 0, link still a symlink, splice round-trip byte-identical, unproject leaves nothing, vendor render still refused, no temp files.
close_reason: Orphan reconciliation implemented and verified, with conservative removal that never deletes a file edited after projection.

title: Decide DCG safety posture: fail-open default, 3 of 103 packs, no config file
description:
Why: dcg is designated the safety boundary beneath all agent harnesses, but its installed posture is entirely built-in defaults and nobody has yet decided whether those defaults are the intended policy. 'dcg doctor' passes — but passing means 'correctly installed', not 'configured as we intend'.

OBSERVED 2026-08-31 (dcg 0.13.9, all read-only checks):

1. NO CONFIG FILE AT ANY LAYER. dcg doctor reports 'USING DEFAULTS'.
     system  /etc/dcg/config.toml            missing (full)
     user    ~/.config/dcg/config.toml       missing (full)
     project /home/klaas/src/machine-state/.dcg.toml   missing (enforcement-only)

2. FAIL-OPEN. 'Fail closed: false'. On unparseable hook input dcg ALLOWS the command. For a
   component whose stated role is a safety boundary, defaulting to allow on confusion is a
   posture worth deciding deliberately rather than inheriting. DCG_FAIL_CLOSED=1 flips it.

3. THREE OF 103 PACKS ENABLED: core.filesystem, core.git, system.disk. Everything else is off,
   including the egress and guardrail-tampering families. Empirically core.filesystem works —
   it blocked an rm -rf during this session.

4. WIRED FOR ONE HARNESS. The dcg hook exists only in ~/.claude/settings.json (user-global,
   PreToolUse). Nothing is broken today, because Claude is the only supported harness installed.
   But the stated intent is that dcg applies REGARDLESS of which agent operates, and wiring a
   newly installed harness is a separate manual 'dcg install' step. Intent is currently
   satisfiable but unverified for any future harness.

5. NO ALLOWLIST ENTRIES. Hook self-heal on, evaluation budget 1000 ms.

DECISIONS REQUIRED:
  a. Fail-open or fail-closed?
  b. Which pack set is the intended baseline for this machine?
  c. Does the intended posture live in a user config (~/.config/dcg/config.toml, full control)
     or a project .dcg.toml (enforcement-only, and therefore projectable by machine-state)?
  d. Should ms status FAIL when a supported harness is installed but not dcg-wired?

Out of scope for substrate v0.01: this is safety policy content, not substrate plumbing. Filed
standalone so it stays visible rather than bloating the v0.01 epic.
design:
(c) is the interesting one for the substrate. A project-level .dcg.toml is enforcement-only — it can tighten but not loosen — which makes it safe to project from canonical: a projected file that can only ever increase restriction cannot become an attack on the safety boundary. A user-level config has full control and therefore should NOT be projected without more thought.

(d) is where the 'applies regardless of harness' intent becomes testable rather than aspirational: the check is per-harness, not global. Answering yes turns a manual install step into a verified invariant.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of (a)-(d) answered and recorded.
- If a config file is adopted, its intended contents are recorded in canonical/tooling/dcg.md Intent, and dcg doctor still passes afterwards.
- No change to dcg configuration is made before the decision is recorded.
notes:
Discovered while writing the canonical tooling record in machine-state-9tw.6. Verification command for all of the above: 'dcg doctor', 'dcg config', 'dcg packs'.

APPLIED 2026-08-31, partially. ~/.config/dcg/config.toml now exists (64 lines); dcg doctor reports all checks passed with the user config loaded and 7 packs enabled.

ANSWERED:
(a) fail-open -> FAIL-CLOSED. A fail-open bypass is silent; a fail-closed error is loud and recoverable. Note: fail_closed IS a valid [general] config key even though 'dcg init' does not document it; the DCG_FAIL_CLOSED env var did not show up in 'dcg config', so the config file is the reliable path.
(b) packs -> enable by INSTALLED SURFACE. Added package_managers, system.services, system.permissions, secret_disclosure, matching pacman, uwsm-managed systemd user units, HOME, and private keys. Cloud/kubernetes/containers/database/infrastructure/windows/cicd stay off; rules for absent software protect nothing and only misfire. Correction to an earlier claim: the previous '3 of 103' was not a choice at all — core is always on and cannot be disabled, and system.disk is on by default.
(c) layer -> USER config, hand-applied, NOT projected. That layer can loosen as well as tighten, so projecting it would let a bad edit in canonical/ silently weaken the boundary. A project .dcg.toml is enforcement-only and would be safe to project if per-repo tightening is ever wanted.

ALSO: observability was off entirely — no log file, and history disabled, so 'dcg history analyze' was reading an empty database and recommending that core be disabled for inactivity on the same day core blocked two real commands. Both now enabled; history recording confirmed working.

STAGED ROLLOUT: the four new packs are set to 'warn' in [policy.packs] while core and system.disk keep denying. Verified empirically — a package_managers pattern returns 'WARN (policy allows)' while core.git force-push returns 'BLOCKED'. Note that [policy.packs] modes are NOT visible in 'dcg config' output; 'dcg test' against a matching pattern is the only way to confirm a pack's mode.

STILL OPEN, which is why this bead stays open:
- Promote the four packs from warn to deny once the log shows what they match. Give it a week of normal work. Removing those four lines is the last step of this decision, not a new one.
- (d) whether ms status should fail when an installed harness is not dcg-wired. Needs a projector change, not config.

(d) ANSWERED AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-01. Yes, ms status now fails when an installed harness is not covered by the guard.

Design: harness records may declare an optional 'wiring' command. Present but unwired prints ** UNGUARDED ** and makes ms status exit non-zero. Absent harnesses are skipped — what is not installed cannot be unguarded, so Codex raises no false alarm. state/tooling.json records a 'guarded' boolean alongside the version.

Verified by negative control, not just by passing: pointing DCG_CONFIG at a nonexistent file makes the wiring check fail, claude reports UNGUARDED, and ms status exits 1. Restoring it returns exit 0.

LATENT BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN ALREADY-SHIPPED WORK: plain 'dcg doctor' exits 0 EVEN WHEN ITS CHECKS FAIL; only --strict signals through the exit code. The dcg record was using plain 'dcg doctor', so the Safety line could never have reported a problem — it would have shown 'active' with the guard broken. Now 'dcg doctor --strict', and the negative control shows 'degraded' correctly. A tooling record that looked green for the wrong reason is precisely the failure these records exist to prevent.

CODEX GAP RECORDED, NOT FAKED: dcg install has flags for Claude, Grok, agy, OpenCode and omp but NONE for Codex, and dcg doctor only inspects Claude's hook registration. Nothing can currently prove Codex would be guarded. codex.md declares no wiring key and says why, and states that establishing wiring is part of installing Codex rather than an afterthought.

KNOWN OVERLAP, deliberately recorded in claude.md: Claude's wiring check is the same command as the dcg record's check, because dcg's doctor is Claude-specific today. The two lines answer different questions — is the guard healthy, versus is THIS HARNESS guarded — and will diverge as soon as a second harness exists. Documented so it is not later 'cleaned up' as duplication.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD: promote the four packs from warn to deny once the log justifies it.

title: Canonical tooling records + derived tooling inventory
description:
Why: beads and dcg ARE part of the substrate, but their generated files are vendor-owned and must never become canonical policy. The clean separation is that machine-state records WHAT A TOOL IS FOR and WHAT WE INTEND, and verifies the installed integration satisfies it — it does not absorb the tool's own output.

What: canonical/tooling/<tool>.md, one per substrate tool. Each record carries five fixed sections:
  Function     - what the tool does, in two or three lines
  Role         - why it is part of this substrate
  Ownership    - which paths the tool owns (VENDOR) and which we own
  Intent       - the policy we require of the installed integration
  Verification - the exact command that checks Intent, and what output counts as satisfied

v0.01 ships two records:

canonical/tooling/beads.md
  Function: durable issue tracking and shared work memory; local Dolt DB, git-backed sync.
  Role: coordination layer. The task system all resident agents share.
  Ownership: VENDOR owns CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md marker blocks, .claude/settings.json,
    .codex/*, .agents/skills/beads/**, .beads/**. We own our own marker block only.
  Verification: 'bd setup claude --check' and 'bd setup codex --check' (must be run with cwd
    inside the repo — the -C flag is ignored by --check).

canonical/tooling/dcg.md
  Function: Destructive Command Guard — a pre-execution shell hook that intercepts potentially
    destructive commands. Supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor,
    Hermes, OpenCode and omp.
  Role: the safety boundary BENEATH the agent harnesses. It applies regardless of which
    supported agent is operating, which is what makes agents interchangeable without
    renegotiating safety each time.
  Ownership: VENDOR owns the dcg binary, its hook registration in ~/.claude/settings.json, and
    ~/.config/dcg/**. We own the recorded intent and the verification, plus (future) a project
    .dcg.toml, which dcg treats as enforcement-only.
  Verification: 'dcg doctor' — all checks must pass and hook wiring must report exactly one
    dcg hook registered.

INVENTORY DECISION: keep versions OUT of BASELINE.md. BASELINE.md is a frozen point-in-time
capture ('Captured 2026-08-30') and it already demonstrates the failure mode — it records
dcg 0.13.9 and Claude Code 2.1.251 but has no entry for bd, because it was written twelve
minutes before 'bd init' existed. Instead: state/tooling.json, DERIVED, regenerated by ms status.
canonical/tooling/*.md says what should be true; state/tooling.json records what is true. Same
canonical-versus-derived split the rest of the substrate rests on.

Observed at time of writing (2026-08-31): bd 1.2.2, dcg 0.13.9, claude 2.1.251, codex absent.
design:
The important move is that a tooling record is not prose — it is a DECLARED CHECK. The Verification section names a command and its success condition, and ms status runs it. That is what stops these records rotting into stale documentation, which is exactly what BASELINE.md did within a day.

Both tools conveniently expose a first-class check already: 'bd setup <recipe> --check' and 'dcg doctor'. A tool with no such check does not get a hand-rolled probe; it gets a record whose Verification section says 'none available', so the gap is visible rather than papered over.
acceptance_criteria:
- canonical/tooling/beads.md and canonical/tooling/dcg.md exist, each with all five sections.
- Every path named in an Ownership section matches the ownership table in machine-state-9tw.2.
- Each Verification section names a runnable command and its success condition.
- state/tooling.json is generated, not hand-written, and BASELINE.md is left unmodified.
- No vendor-generated content is copied into canonical/.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-08-31: four records, not the two the bead specified — canonical/tooling/{beads,dcg,claude,codex}.md. The two harness records were added so ms status produces the Harnesses group from the original sketch; without them the substrate would describe its tools but not its tenants.

Each record carries the five sections (Function, Role, Ownership, Intent, Verification) plus a fenced toml block that ms status executes. Ownership sections were checked line by line against the table in machine-state-9tw.2.

ONE PROJECTOR CHANGE: ms status gained an optional 'missing' label, used when a check command cannot be executed at all. 'The tool is absent' and 'the tool's check failed' are different facts, and codex needed the distinction to report 'not installed' rather than 'unknown'.

ONE CORRECTION DURING WRITING: beads.md and claude.md initially both ran 'bd setup claude --check', reporting one fact under two names. beads.md now verifies that the tracker itself is operational (bd stats); harness integration is verified in the harness records where it belongs.

INVENTORY: state/tooling.json is generated by ms status and holds all four tools. BASELINE.md is untouched, as intended — it stays a frozen capture.

ms status output is now:
  Coordination  beads 1.2.2 operational
  Harnesses     claude 2.1.251 integration stale / codex - not installed
  Safety        dcg 0.13.9 active

Groups print in alphabetical order rather than the sketch's Coordination/Safety/Harnesses. Ordering them semantically would mean hardcoding group names in the projector, which the agent-neutral rule forbids; alphabetical is deterministic and needs no mechanism. Noted rather than fixed.

TWO REAL CONDITIONS SURFACED, both pre-existing and neither invented by this bead: the claude integration is stale (filed separately as vendor maintenance), and dcg's posture is inherited defaults (machine-state-3r1). dcg.md says outright that 'dcg doctor' passing means correctly installed, not configured as intended.

Acceptance test re-run after all changes: 11/11.

FALSIFICATION AUDIT 2026-09-01. Every check declared by a tooling record has now been proven able to fail, using selective PATH shims in a scratch copy so the live inventory was never polluted.

  beads / bd stats                 -> 'database unreachable'      (shim: bd stats exits 1)
  claude / bd setup claude --check -> 'integration stale'         (shim: bd setup exits 1)
  codex  / codex --version         -> 'present but not responding' (shim: codex on PATH, exits 3)
                                      vs 'not installed' when genuinely absent
  dcg    / dcg doctor --strict     -> 'degraded'                   (proven earlier)
  claude / wiring                  -> ** UNGUARDED **, exit 1      (proven earlier)

The codex result is the interesting one: it confirms the fail/missing distinction is real rather than decorative. A broken-but-present tool and an absent tool report differently, which is what the 'missing' key was added for.

EXIT-CODE CONTRACT, previously undocumented and now in SUBSTRATE.md section 5: only a SAFETY failure is fatal. An unguarded harness exits non-zero; a down tracker, a stale vendor integration, or an unresponsive tool are reported on their line and exit 0. Verified empirically — all three health failures exit 0, only the broken guard exits 1. The split is deliberate: an agent operating without a guard is a different class of problem from an integration that has drifted, and the stale claude integration sat for a day where reporting it was sufficient to get it fixed.

SUBSTRATE.md now also states the general rule: every check must be verified to FAIL, not merely to pass. A check that cannot fail reports green for the wrong reason — which already happened once here, when the dcg record used plain 'dcg doctor', a command that exits 0 even when its own checks fail.
close_reason: Four tooling records written with executable Verification blocks; ms status renders all three groups and generates state/tooling.json. BASELINE.md untouched.

title: Write claude and codex adapter manifests
description:
Why: the adapters are where 'interchangeable agents' stops being a slogan — two agents, two manifests, zero agent-specific code in the projector.

TARGETS ARE NOT YET DECIDABLE. The previously planned targets (./CLAUDE.md and ./AGENTS.md as render targets) are withdrawn: both files are VENDOR-owned output of 'bd setup', and pointing our projector at them would fight bd's installer. See machine-state-9tw.2, which must resolve the composition seam first.

What survives from the earlier plan, unchanged:
  link  ~/.claude/skills  from canonical/skills
This target is safe and confirmed: ~/.claude/ has no skills/ directory, and 'bd setup claude --check' shows bd's claude recipe installs only the SessionStart hook in .claude/settings.json — it does not claim ~/.claude/skills.

What this bead writes once 9tw.2 lands:
- adapters/claude.toml and adapters/codex.toml, using only the three documented keys.
- Render targets chosen from the composition seam that 9tw.2 establishes, NOT from vendor-owned files.

Codex still gets the smaller manifest: ~/.codex/ does not exist on this machine, so its only present integration surface is in-repo.
design:
Explicitly NOT touching, in v0.01: global ~/.claude/settings.json (hand-written, holds the dcg PreToolUse hook — the FOREIGN case), and every bd-owned path (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/settings.json, .codex/*, .agents/skills/beads/*) — the VENDOR case.

The projector's refusal path now has two distinct classes to refuse on, not one. That is a strengthening of the original design, not a change to it: FOREIGN (a human wrote it) and VENDOR (another installer owns it) both mean 'not ours, do not write'.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both manifests parse with tomllib and use only the three documented keys.
- No manifest target is a vendor-owned path, per the ownership table from machine-state-9tw.2.
- Every source path referenced exists in canonical/.
- ~ expands correctly; no target resolves outside the repo or ~/.claude.
- The manifests contain no logic, no conditionals, no agent-specific code paths.
notes:
TARGET CORRECTION from machine-state-9tw.2: do NOT link the ~/.claude/skills container. Link individual skill directories (~/.claude/skills/<name>) — own the smallest addressable region, never the container. Same reason bd owns .agents/skills/beads/ rather than .agents/skills/.

Render targets are now resolved: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are reachable after all, but via kind='splice' with marker 'MACHINE-STATE POLICY', never kind='render'. See the ownership table and seam decision in machine-state-9tw.2.

DELIVERED 2026-08-31: adapters/claude.toml (splice ./CLAUDE.md + link ~/.claude/skills/machine-state) and adapters/codex.toml (splice ./AGENTS.md). Three targets total.

Validated: both parse with tomllib; only the five documented keys used; every source exists; no vendor path under render or link.

Projected end to end in a scratch copy with HOME redirected to a fake home, so the real ~/.claude was never touched:
- All three targets created; ms diff exit 0; idempotent and hash-stable over three runs.
- Byte-check: everything outside our region in BOTH CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md is identical to the committed vendor file. bd's one block in CLAUDE.md and both blocks in AGENTS.md intact.
- unproject restored both vendor files to their exact committed sha and left the fake ~/.claude/skills empty.

BIDIRECTIONAL CO-TENANCY PROVEN, the result this whole design rests on: after our splice, running the vendor installers (bd setup claude, bd setup codex) on top left OUR marker block intact in both files, ms diff still reported in-sync, and bd setup claude --check reported its own integration as current. Each tool rewrites only its own region and tolerates the other's. The seam works in both directions, not just ours.
close_reason: Both manifests written, validated, and projected end to end in a sandboxed home. Bidirectional co-tenancy with bd's installers proven.

title: Acceptance test: canonical is truth, projections are derived
description:
Why: one test for the one invariant. If this passes, the substrate is real and agents are interchangeable tenants of it. If it cannot be written, the architecture is wrong.

tests/acceptance.sh — one script, one exit code, five assertions:

1. PROJECT      From a clean tree, ms project realises every target in both manifests. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md exist and now share their common policy fragments byte-for-byte. ~/.claude/skills is a symlink into canonical/skills.
2. IDEMPOTENT   ms project again changes nothing: state/projection.json is unchanged, no file mtime-churn beyond the manifest, no temp files.
3. DRIFT        Append a line to the projected CLAUDE.md. ms diff MUST exit non-zero and name CLAUDE.md. This is the assertion the whole architecture rests on.
4. RESTORE      ms project returns CLAUDE.md to canonical byte-for-byte; the hand-edit is gone. Canonical wins, always.
5. FOREIGN      Point a scratch adapter at a pre-existing unmanaged file. ms project MUST refuse and leave the file untouched. The substrate does not clobber what it did not create.

Then ms unproject, and assert nothing managed remains outside the repo.

Assertions 3 and 5 are the load-bearing ones: they prove drift is detectable and first contact is safe. A substrate that only proves its happy path has proved nothing.
design:
No root, no network, no external service. The test must be runnable offline on this machine and on a fresh checkout.

The test restores ~/.claude to its pre-test condition regardless of outcome (trap), since it is the one target outside the repo.

Verify once during implementation that assertion 3 genuinely fails when drift detection is disabled — an assertion that cannot fail is not one.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/acceptance.sh exits 0 on this machine, printing one line per assertion.
- Assertions 3 and 5 verified to fail when their mechanism is deliberately disabled; recorded in bead notes.
- The test leaves no scratch adapters, no drift, and ~/.claude exactly as found.
- First passing run recorded in the epic before it closes.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-08-31. FIRST PASSING RUN: 11/11 assertions, exit 0. Stable across three consecutive runs.

  1a project realises every target
  1b the HOME crossing is a symlink into canonical
  1c both harnesses receive the shared fragments byte-for-byte
  1d each vendor file is untouched outside our region
  2  a second project changes nothing
  3  drift is detected and names the file
  4  canonical wins: the edit is gone, byte-for-byte
  5  a file we never created is refused, not clobbered
  6  unproject restores the vendor files exactly and leaves nothing
  3n assertion 3 fails when drift detection is disabled
  5n assertion 5 fails when the refusal is disabled

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, as required: 3n patches inspect() so splice always reports OK, then confirms tampering goes unreported; 5n patches may_write() to return True, then confirms the foreign file IS clobbered. Both assertions therefore can fail, so passing them means something.

DEVIATION: the file is tests/acceptance.py, not tests/acceptance.sh. Python was already a hard dependency (bin/ms is Python), the assertions are byte-level comparisons that bash makes awkward, and writing them in Python avoids shell quoting hazards entirely. Substance is unchanged: one script, one exit code, five assertions plus teardown.

DESIGN CHANGE from the bead: the test is HERMETIC rather than run against the live tree with a trap. It builds a throwaway copy of the repo with HOME redirected into the sandbox, so it touches neither the real ~/.claude nor the working tree, and needs no trap to be safe. Verified after three runs: no leftover sandboxes in /tmp, ~/.claude/skills still does not exist, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md still byte-identical to HEAD, working tree carries only intended new files. The bead's criterion that ~/.claude be left exactly as found is met by never touching it.
close_reason: tests/acceptance.py written and passing 11/11, including two negative controls. Hermetic: no leftover sandboxes, real ~/.claude and working tree untouched.

title: Create canonical tree and adapter manifest schema
description:
Why: fix the layout and the manifest format before anything is written into them, so the projector and the adapters have a stable contract.

What:

canonical/policy/         agent-neutral operating rules, as numbered fragments
canonical/skills/         agent-neutral skill trees (shape follows .agents/skills/beads)
canonical/desktop/        RESERVED, empty with a .gitkeep and a README line — future home for hypr/ and noctalia/
adapters/                 one <agent>.toml per agent
state/projection.json     the projection manifest (written by the projector, tracked in git)

Adapter manifest schema — deliberately tiny, three keys per target:

  [[target]]
  kind    = "render" | "link"
  path    = destination, absolute or repo-relative
  sources = ordered list of canonical paths (render) or a single canonical dir (link)

No conditionals, no templating language, no per-agent code. If an adapter needs logic, the design is wrong.
design:
canonical/policy as ordered fragments rather than one file is what makes divergent projection possible: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md can select different fragment sets while sharing the ones that matter. This is the whole reason the two files drifted by hand.

desktop/ ships empty on purpose. An empty reserved slot proves the layout anticipated Hyprland and Noctalia; adding them later must not require moving anything.
acceptance_criteria:
- Directories exist with .gitkeep where empty; state/projection.json is gitignored-exempt (tracked).
- adapters/ contains a schema comment or README documenting exactly the three keys, with one worked example.
- No projector code and no canonical content added by this bead.
notes:
Manifest schema gains a third kind (see machine-state-9tw.3):
  kind = "render" | "link" | "splice"
splice targets need one extra key naming the marker pair, e.g.
  marker = "MACHINE-STATE POLICY"
rendered by the projector into the same BEGIN/END comment form bd uses. Still no conditionals and no per-agent logic.

Layout gains a tooling slot (see machine-state-9tw.6):
  canonical/tooling/       one <tool>.md record per substrate tool (beads, dcg)
  state/tooling.json       DERIVED inventory, regenerated by ms status — never hand-edited
Versions deliberately do NOT go in BASELINE.md: that file is a frozen capture and already
omits bd, having been written twelve minutes before bd init ran.

DELIVERED 2026-08-31. Created: canonical/{policy,policy/agents,skills,tooling}/ with .gitkeep, canonical/desktop/README.md (reservation note), adapters/README.md (schema + worked example), state/projection.json (schema 1, empty targets).

SCHEMA DECISION — a fifth key. splice targets need to know how to wrap their marker, since comment syntax differs by format (Markdown <!-- -->, TOML/shell #, Lua --). Rather than infer it from the file extension — which is exactly the content-awareness the projector is forbidden to have — the manifest states it: comment = 'html' | 'hash' | 'dash'. So: three keys on every target (kind, path, sources), plus marker and comment on splice.

SUBSTRATE.md §3 updated to match; the contract now also points at adapters/README.md for the full schema.

The worked example in adapters/README.md was verified to parse with tomllib and yield three targets (render/link/splice).

NOT created here, deliberately: bin/ (machine-state-9tw.3), tests/ (machine-state-9tw.5), any canonical policy or tooling content (machine-state-9tw.6 and later), .gitignore changes (nothing yet needs ignoring; SUBSTRATE.md §2 requires appending to it rather than rewriting when the time comes).
close_reason: Canonical tree, adapter manifest schema, and initial projection manifest created. Schema gained a fifth key (comment) for splice targets; SUBSTRATE.md updated to match. No projector code, no canonical content.

title: Write bin/ms projector (project | diff | status | unproject)
description:
Why: the one piece of executable code in v0.01. Everything else is data.

What: single Python 3.14 stdlib script, no dependencies.

  ms project    read every adapters/*.toml, realise each target, update state/projection.json
  ms diff       compare each target against what canonical would produce; exit non-zero on drift, print what differs
  ms status     one line per target: kind, path, in-sync / drifted / missing / foreign
  ms unproject  remove every target this repo owns, per the manifest; leave nothing behind

Mechanisms:
  render - concatenate ordered source fragments, write atomically (temp + os.replace in the same dir)
  link   - symlink the canonical dir at the target path

SAFETY RULE, non-negotiable: a target is written only if it is absent, or a symlink this repo owns, or byte-identical to what state/projection.json says was last projected. Anything else is FOREIGN — refuse, report, and require an explicit human decision. First contact with a hand-written file must never be a silent overwrite.

Content-agnostic: the projector concatenates and copies bytes. It must not parse markdown, lua, or toml content. tomllib is used only to read adapter manifests.
design:
tomllib is stdlib in 3.11+, so adapters can be TOML with zero dependencies.

os.replace for render keeps a reader from ever seeing a half-written CLAUDE.md. Symlink for link keeps the repo the single source of truth and makes ownership obvious to a human running ls -la.

unproject exists in v0.01 because a substrate you cannot cleanly remove is not something to install on a working machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- All four subcommands work; ms diff exits non-zero on drift and zero when clean.
- The foreign-file refusal is demonstrated: pointing an adapter at a pre-existing unmanaged file causes a refusal, not an overwrite.
- ms project run twice changes nothing the second time (idempotent, no temp files left).
- ms unproject leaves no managed target behind.
- Stdlib only; works from any cwd; contains no sudo, no network, no git invocation.
notes:
OWNERSHIP CLASSES (from machine-state-9tw.2): the safety rule now distinguishes FOREIGN (hand-written by a human) from VENDOR (owned by another tool's installer, e.g. anything bd setup emits). Both are refuse-and-report; they differ only in the remediation the projector suggests — promote to canonical, versus leave to the owning tool. 'ms status' should name the class.

THIRD MECHANISM REQUIRED (from the 9tw.2 experiment): 'splice'.

  render  whole file, we own it entirely        (files we create)
  link    symlink a canonical dir at a target   (trees)
  splice  replace the region between two literal marker strings, preserving everything outside  (files we CO-OWN with a vendor)

splice is what makes co-tenancy with bd possible without a rewrite war. It follows the convention bd itself uses and which the experiment proved bd honours: bd replaces only its own markers and left a foreign block untouched in the same file.

Content-agnosticism is preserved: splice locates two literal delimiter strings and replaces the bytes between them. It does not parse markdown, lua, or toml. That is what lets the same mechanism serve Hyprland .lua and Noctalia .toml later, since both take comment markers.

splice rules:
- If both markers are present, replace between them.
- If absent, APPEND the marked region at end of file (mirrors bd's own behaviour on a markerless file).
- Never touch a byte outside our marker pair.
- unproject removes our marker pair and its content, leaving the rest intact.
- A vendor file is therefore no longer refused outright: it is refused for render/link, permitted for splice. The VENDOR class means 'do not own the file', not 'do not touch the file'.

'ms status' gains grouped output, driven by the Verification section of each canonical/tooling/<tool>.md record. Target shape:

  Coordination
    beads   1.2.2      configured
    export             enabled
  Safety
    dcg     0.13.9     active
  Harnesses
    claude  2.1.251    integrated
    codex   —          not installed

Each line is the RESULT OF RUNNING A DECLARED CHECK, not a hardcoded string: bd setup <recipe> --check for harness integration, dcg doctor for safety, export.auto from .beads/config.yaml for export. A tool whose check cannot run reports 'unknown', never 'ok'. ms status also writes state/tooling.json.

Note the -C trap: bd setup --check ignores -C and reads the real cwd, so ms must chdir before invoking it.

DELIVERED 2026-08-31: bin/ms, 431 lines, stdlib only (hashlib json os pathlib re shlex subprocess sys tempfile tomllib). Exercised against fixtures in a scratch copy; no fixtures in the live repo.

TWO BUGS FOUND BY THE TESTS, both fixed:
1. dest() used Path.resolve(), which follows the FINAL symlink, so a freshly created link target read back as the directory it pointed at and inspect() classified it foreign / exists and is not a symlink. Now resolves the parent chain only and keeps the final component.
2. The link branch of project unlinked the existing symlink BEFORE the needs-rebuilding check, but recreated it only when status was not OK. So a second ms project DELETED the link while printing unchanged. Precisely the failure the idempotency criterion exists to catch. Unlink now happens inside the rebuild branch.

ONE DESIGN CORRECTION: splice originally appended a cosmetic blank line before our BEGIN marker. That byte lives OUTSIDE our marker pair, so unproject could not take it back and the vendor file did not round-trip. Padding removed; we now add only the newline needed to keep BEGIN on its own line. project then unproject is now byte-identical for a vendor file, verified by sha256.

VERIFIED:
- project/diff/status/unproject all work; diff exits 1 on drift, 0 when clean.
- Idempotent across three consecutive project runs; no temp files left.
- Drift detected and restored for BOTH render and splice; another owner's marked block in the same spliced file survived untouched.
- FOREIGN refusal: a pre-existing unmanaged file is refused, left byte-identical, exit 1, and the other targets still project.
- unproject removes render/link/splice regions, skips targets with no record, and empties state/projection.json.
- Runs correctly from cwd=/.
- No git, no sudo, no network, no shell=True.

WRITE RULE AS IMPLEMENTED, reconciling SUBSTRATE.md sections 5 and 6: a target may be written if it is absent, or we hold a record for it (our own drift is ours to restore, canonical wins), or its content already equals what canonical would produce (safe adoption). Only a file that exists, has no record, AND differs is FOREIGN. splice is always permitted since it touches only our own region; that is what makes vendor files reachable.

TOOLING CONVENTION FOR machine-state-9tw.6: ms status reads a fenced toml block inside each canonical/tooling/<tool>.md, with keys group, version, version_re (optional), check, ok, fail. Verified working end to end. Reading our own canonical records is not a projection: the content-agnostic rule constrains what the projector WRITES. Note that bd setup claude --check exits non-zero while the integration is merely STALE, so choose the fail wording accordingly.
close_reason: bin/ms written and exercised: all four subcommands, idempotency, drift detect and restore, foreign refusal, byte-exact unproject round trip. Two bugs found and fixed by the tests (symlink resolution, link idempotency); splice padding removed so vendor files round-trip exactly.

title: Agent-neutral machine-state substrate v0.01
description:
Goal: the shared substrate BENEATH interchangeable resident agents. The resident agents are Claude Code, Codex, and future local agents — we do not write a new agent, we write the ground they stand on.

Core architecture: this repo is the canonical source of truth. Agent-specific locations (~/.claude/, ~/.codex/, repo CLAUDE.md, later ~/.config/hypr and ~/.config/noctalia) are ADAPTERS — one-way projections of canonical state, treated as derived artifacts like build output. Never hand-edited, always regenerable, always removable.

The single invariant v0.01 must prove:
  canonical -> projection is one-way, deterministic, and drift is detectable.

If that holds, adding an agent is adding an adapter manifest, and adding managed config (Hyprland, Noctalia) is adding a canonical directory. Neither touches the projector.
design:
Grounded in probes of this machine (2026-08-31):
- CLAUDE.md (3139B) and AGENTS.md (5926B) have ALREADY DRIFTED — different inodes, different beads blocks. v0.01 repairs a real defect, not a hypothetical one.
- ~/.codex/ does not exist (Codex not installed). The codex adapter therefore targets repo-root AGENTS.md, which Codex reads per-project. Do not invent a home layout for absent software.
- ~/.claude/ has no skills/, agents/, commands/, hooks/ — projecting into it is zero-clobber.
- .agents/skills/beads/{SKILL.md,agents/openai.yaml} is already the neutral-skill + per-agent-adapter pattern. Beads shipped the precedent; follow its shape rather than inventing one.
- ~/.config/hypr (13 .lua under config/ behind hyprland.lua) and ~/.config/noctalia/config.toml are plain unversioned files, no symlinks. They are FUTURE tenants, out of v0.01.
- Omarchy is not installed. We borrow the convention — canonical tree + idempotent refresh commands — not the software.

Two projection mechanisms, and only two, so that everything later is one of them:
  render - canonical fragments composed into an agent-specific file (policy -> CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md)
  link   - a canonical tree exposed verbatim at an agent path (skills -> ~/.claude/skills)
The projector stays content-agnostic: it moves bytes and composes fragments, it never parses markdown, lua, or toml. That is what lets Hyprland and Noctalia join later without touching it.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed and the acceptance test passes: a hand-edit to any projected target is detected by 'ms diff', and 'ms project' restores it to canonical byte-for-byte.
notes:
Replaces the hostwatch framing, which built a new deterministic monitoring program instead of a substrate. Machine telemetry may return later as a TENANT of this substrate, not as its foundation.

PROVENANCE CORRECTION (2026-08-31): the epic's original design cited drifted CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the motivating real defect. That motivation is withdrawn. Both files came from commit 4d81b55 'bd init', are byte-identical to it, and were never hand-edited; their difference is bd template-version skew between two recipe installs, not policy drift. 'bd setup claude --check' currently reports CLAUDE.md as stale and offers to regenerate it.

The architecture survives; its motivating example was wrong. A THIRD ownership class is added:
  CANONICAL - authored by us (README.md, BASELINE.md; no policy content exists yet)
  VENDOR    - owned by another tool's installer (everything bd setup emits)
  PROJECTED - derived by bin/ms from canonical
The substrate must not fight vendor installers for files they own. This makes the projector's refusal path load-bearing rather than theoretical.
close_reason: v0.01 complete: 9/9 children closed, acceptance test 11/11, substrate projected onto this machine and verified in-sync. Tagged v0.01-seed at the last pre-projection commit.

title: Acceptance test: prove the substrate works and the boundary holds
description:
Why: one test is the whole point of v0.01. If it passes, the substrate is real; if it cannot be written, the design was wrong.

What: tests/acceptance.sh — one script, one pass/fail, three assertions.

LIVENESS
  Delete state/hostwatch/latest.json, then: systemctl --user start machine-state-hostwatch.service
  Within 30s latest.json exists again, parses as JSON, has schema==1, and collected_at is within 60s of now.

CONFINEMENT (write boundary)
  Run the same unit with an override whose ExecStart attempts a write to $HOME/ms-boundary-probe.
  The write MUST fail (EROFS/EACCES) and the file must not exist afterwards.

CONFINEMENT (network boundary)
  Run the same unit with an override whose ExecStart attempts socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM).
  It MUST fail with EAFNOSUPPORT/EPERM. No DNS, no connect, nothing that needs a live network to decide.

The test cleans up its own overrides. It asserts the sandbox denies things, not merely that the happy path works — a substrate whose boundary is untested is a boundary that does not exist.
design:
Both confinement probes run through the real unit via systemd drop-in overrides, so the test exercises the shipped sandbox rather than a re-declaration of it. Probes are inline python -c one-liners; no probe scripts to leave lying around.

The test must not require network, root, or an external service, so it stays runnable on a plane.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/acceptance.sh exits 0 on this machine after bin/ms-agent install, and prints one line per assertion.
- Deliberately breaking the sandbox (removing RestrictAddressFamilies) makes the test fail — verified once during implementation and recorded in bead notes.
- The test leaves no drop-in overrides, probe files, or altered unit state behind.
- Result of the first passing run is recorded in the epic before closing it.
close_reason: Superseded by machine-state-9tw: hostwatch was a new monitoring program, not the substrate beneath existing agents.

title: Write hostwatch collector (agents/hostwatch/run.py)
description:
Why: the resident payload. Deterministic stand-in for a future agent brain; proves the write path and the sandbox without needing an LLM.

What: single-file Python 3.14 stdlib script, no imports outside the stdlib, no argparse ceremony.

Collects a deliberately tiny read-only fact set:
- timestamp (UTC, ISO-8601), hostname, kernel release
- uptime seconds (/proc/uptime)
- load average (os.getloadavg)
- memory total/available (/proc/meminfo)
- root filesystem free bytes (os.statvfs on /)
- battery percent + AC state if /sys/class/power_supply exists, else null

Writes state/hostwatch/latest.json atomically (write temp in the same dir, os.replace). Repo root resolved from the script's own path, not from cwd or an env var.

On any collection error: still write a valid document with the failing field null and an 'errors' list. The agent must never leave a half-written or missing state file.
design:
Atomic replace matters because a human or a future reader may read latest.json at any moment, including mid-run. Same-directory temp keeps the rename on one filesystem (btrfs subvolume @home).

Schema is versioned from day one: top-level 'schema': 1. Cheap now, unavoidable later.
acceptance_criteria:
- python3 agents/hostwatch/run.py writes a valid JSON document to state/hostwatch/latest.json.
- Document contains schema, collected_at, and every field above; missing sources yield null plus an entry in errors, never a crash.
- Script is stdlib-only and works when run from any cwd.
- Running it twice leaves exactly one state file, no temp files behind.
close_reason: Superseded by machine-state-9tw: hostwatch was a new monitoring program, not the substrate beneath existing agents.

title: Write hardened systemd --user unit and timer
description:
Why: the sandbox IS the trust boundary. The unit file is where the permission model is actually enforced, rather than merely described.

What: systemd/machine-state-hostwatch.service (Type=oneshot) and .timer.

Service sandbox, at minimum:
  NoNewPrivileges=yes
  PrivateTmp=yes
  ProtectSystem=strict
  ProtectHome=read-only
  ReadWritePaths=/home/klaas/src/machine-state/state
  ProtectKernelTunables=yes
  ProtectControlGroups=yes
  RestrictSUIDSGID=yes
  RestrictNamespaces=yes
  LockPersonality=yes
  MemoryDenyWriteExecute=yes
  SystemCallFilter=@system-service
  RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX
  UMask=0077

Timer: OnStartupSec plus OnUnitActiveSec (15min), Persistent=false. No linger, so it only ticks inside a live session.
design:
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX is chosen over IPAddressDeny for the network boundary: it is seccomp-enforced and therefore reliable in a --user unit, whereas IPAddressDeny needs BPF cgroup delegation that user scope may not have. It also fails loudly and testably (socket(AF_INET) raises), which the acceptance test depends on.

VERIFY during implementation: that ReadWritePaths= does in fact re-open the state dir read-write underneath ProtectHome=read-only in systemd 261. If it does not, drop ProtectHome and rely on ProtectSystem=strict plus ReadWritePaths, and record the change in SUBSTRATE.md.

Also verify @system-service does not block the atomic-replace path or /proc reads.
acceptance_criteria:
- systemd-analyze verify passes on both units.
- systemd-analyze security scores the service and the exposure level is recorded in the bead notes.
- Timer schedule is 15 minutes, non-persistent, no linger required.
- Unit references the repo paths only; no ExecStart outside the repo.
close_reason: Superseded by machine-state-9tw: hostwatch was a new monitoring program, not the substrate beneath existing agents.

title: Create substrate repo skeleton
description:
Why: fix the layout before writing anything into it, so the sandbox profile and install script have stable paths to name.

What: create the directory layout and placeholders only.

agents/hostwatch/     - the single v0.01 agent
systemd/              - unit + timer source of truth (repo-owned)
state/hostwatch/      - the ONLY writable path for agents
bin/                  - install/uninstall helper
tests/                - acceptance test

Add .gitignore rules: state/**/*.log is ignored, state/**/latest.json is tracked (state is the reported artifact; logs are noise). Add state/hostwatch/.gitkeep.
acceptance_criteria:
- The five directories exist with a .gitkeep where empty.
- .gitignore ignores agent run logs but not latest.json.
- No executable code added by this bead.

title: Resident-agent substrate v0.01
description:
Goal: the smallest end-to-end loop that proves a resident agent can live on this workstation — scheduled by the user session, sandboxed, observing read-only, and reporting into this repo. Not a distro, not a framework, not an agent runtime.

v0.01 proves the PLUMBING, not the reasoning. The resident payload is a deterministic stdlib-Python collector standing in for a future agent brain; swapping in an LLM is a later version. If the substrate is right, that swap touches one file.

Shape: one agent (hostwatch) + one systemd --user timer + one sandbox profile + one state file + one acceptance test.
design:
Constraints from BASELINE.md and live probes:
- systemd 261, +SECCOMP +BPF_FRAMEWORK; user manager present; Linger=no (agent lives only inside the login session — deliberate for v0.01).
- Python 3.14.7 stdlib only. No node/go/rust/docker, no pip, no venv, no AUR packages.
- fish login shell, Hyprland/Wayland via uwsm; agent must not depend on the compositor.
- Repo is at /home/klaas/src/machine-state; conservative git profile (no agent-initiated commits).

Boring option at every fork: oneshot + timer, not a daemon. Files, not IPC. JSON, not a database. One agent, not a registry.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads closed, and the acceptance test in the final child passes on this machine from a clean checkout + install.
notes: Supersedes the open-ended framing of the original definition bead. Deferred scope is recorded in the SUBSTRATE.md non-goals section, not spread across beads.

title: Write SUBSTRATE.md — the canonical/adapter contract
description:
Why: the substrate is a set of conventions. If they are not written in one place, every future agent, adapter, and managed config re-invents them. This document is the contract the projector and every adapter implement against.

What: SUBSTRATE.md at repo root, roughly two screens, stating concrete choices:

1. CANONICAL — the repo is the source of truth. canonical/ holds agent-neutral content: policy/ (operating rules), skills/ (neutral SKILL.md trees). desktop/ is reserved for Hyprland and Noctalia, empty in v0.01.
2. ADAPTERS — adapters/<agent>.toml declares that agent's targets. An adapter is a manifest, never content. Adding an agent = adding a manifest.
3. PROJECTION — exactly two mechanisms, render and link. One-way, canonical to target. Targets are derived artifacts: regenerable, removable, never hand-edited.
4. DRIFT — every projection is recorded in state/projection.json with source and target hashes. A hand-edit is a detectable, reportable condition, not a merge.
5. PROMOTION — the reverse path (target edit back into canonical) is deliberately manual and human-initiated. The substrate never guesses that a hand-edit was intentional.
6. BOUNDARY — what the projector may touch, and what requires a human.
7. NON-GOALS — the deferred list for v0.01.

Definition-only bead: no canonical/, no adapters/, no bin/ms.
design:
This doc supersedes the ad-hoc convention currently implied by the repo (two hand-mirrored instruction files, an .agents/ tree, and a .claude/ dir with no stated relationship between them). It should name that existing arrangement and say which parts become canonical and which become projections.

Write it so a future agent that has never seen this conversation can rebuild the substrate from the document alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- SUBSTRATE.md exists at repo root and covers all seven sections.
- Each section states one concrete choice with a one-line reason, not a survey of options.
- Explicitly resolves the status of the existing CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .agents/, .claude/ and .codex/ paths: which becomes canonical, which becomes a projection.
- NON-GOALS includes at minimum: no reverse auto-sync, no agent-initiated git, no root or sudo, no network, no package installs, no desktop config in v0.01, no multi-machine.
- No directories or code created by this bead.
notes:
Rewritten twice: first from an open-ended 'where should things live' bead, then from the hostwatch framing. Now scoped to the canonical/adapter architecture.

DELIVERED 2026-08-31: SUBSTRATE.md, 206 lines, 9 sections.

DEVIATION FROM ACCEPTANCE: the bead specified seven sections and 'roughly two screens'. Shipped nine sections and roughly four. The two extra sections are Ownership (§2) and Tooling (§7), which did not exist when this bead was written — they were required by machine-state-9tw.2 (ownership classes, seam) and machine-state-9tw.6 (tooling records) after the fact. §2 in particular is demanded by this bead's own acceptance criterion that the status of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.agents/.claude/.codex be explicitly resolved, which needs a table. Length was not trimmed by cutting required content.

Verified: all seven required non-goals present; all five named paths classified; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md still byte-identical to 4d81b55; only SUBSTRATE.md created.
close_reason: SUBSTRATE.md written at repo root (206 lines, 9 sections). All acceptance criteria verified: every named path classified, all seven required non-goals present, no directories or code created.

title: Phase 2: bring Noctalia under canonical/desktop
description:
Deferred deliberately when Hyprland was projected on 2026-09-01. Noctalia is a harder case and should not be forced into Hyprland's shape.

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT:
- Single ~/.config/noctalia/config.toml, no include or drop-in mechanism found. Hyprland's require() chain is what made the clean 'our own module, loaded last' design possible; Noctalia has no equivalent.
- TOML makes duplicate keys an ERROR, so splice cannot override a value the way a later Lua call can. Owning a marker region in that file would not let us change a setting.
- The config is very likely APP-WRITTEN: 58 machine-formatted setting lines, and Noctalia is a GUI shell with a settings panel. If it rewrites config.toml when a setting changes, canonicalizing it makes every UI tweak drift, and ms project would overwrite the user's changes. That is the bd problem with no marker escape hatch.
- Not package-owned (pacman owns /usr/bin/noctalia at 5.0.0_beta.10-1.1, but not the config).

FIRST QUESTION, before any design: does Noctalia rewrite its own config.toml? Change a setting in its UI and watch the file. If it does, the honest answer may be that it is not canonicalizable yet, and the record should say so — like the Codex wiring gap.

'noctalia config' has validate and replay helpers worth investigating; a validate command would make a good tooling-record check regardless of whether the file becomes managed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Established empirically whether Noctalia rewrites config.toml.
- Either a design that survives that answer, or a recorded decision that it is not canonicalizable yet, with the reason.
- canonical/tooling/noctalia.md exists either way.

title: Your hypr config is a frozen copy of a package-maintained template
description:
~/.config/hypr was copied from /etc/skel/.config/hypr at account creation. That skel tree is owned by the package cachyos-hypr-noctalia (1.2.5-1 today) and moves with upgrades; your copy does not, and nothing reports the divergence.

They are identical today, verified 2026-09-01 — apart from canonical/desktop/hypr/machine-state.lua, which is ours. So this is not a problem yet. It becomes one silently, which is the same shape as the stale bd claude integration that sat unnoticed for a day until a tooling record turned it into a check.

Worth a check that compares ~/.config/hypr/config against /etc/skel/.config/hypr/config and reports files that have diverged, ignoring machine-state.lua. Now that the two decisions live in our own module and the template files are pristine, any difference at all is either a package update worth adopting or an unrecorded hand-edit — both things you want to see.

Not urgent. File it before it matters rather than discover it after.
acceptance_criteria:
- A check exists that reports divergence between ~/.config/hypr/config and the skel template.
- machine-state.lua is excluded from the comparison.
- Wired into a tooling record so ms status surfaces it, or explicitly deferred with a reason.

title: Refresh the stale bd claude integration in CLAUDE.md
description:
ms status now surfaces this on every run: the claude harness reports 'integration stale'.

bd setup claude --check reports CLAUDE.md as installed but STALE. Its block carries template hash 6cd5cc61 while the current template is 970c3bf2 — the same skew found during the machine-state-9tw.2 provenance investigation, present since bd init on 2026-08-30 and never addressed. The only content difference is one line (bd dolt push) in the session-close snippet.

Fix: run 'bd setup claude' with the working directory inside the repo. It rewrites only bd's own marker block; the experiment in machine-state-9tw.2 confirmed all out-of-marker content survives, and machine-state-9tw.4 confirmed our MACHINE-STATE POLICY region survives it too.

VENDOR MAINTENANCE, not substrate work: this is invoking bd's own installer on a file bd owns. Kept separate from the v0.01 epic deliberately.

Note the -C trap: bd setup <recipe> --check ignores -C and inspects the real cwd, so cd into the repo rather than passing -C.
acceptance_criteria:
- bd setup claude --check reports CLAUDE.md as current.
- ms status shows the claude harness as integrated.
- Our MACHINE-STATE POLICY region, if projected by then, is intact afterwards.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-31. Ran 'bd setup claude' with cwd inside the repo. Output: 'Updated existing beads section in CLAUDE.md'.

The diff was exactly two lines, both inside bd's own marker block, and exactly what the machine-state-9tw.2 provenance investigation predicted:
  hash 6cd5cc61 -> 970c3bf2
  + 'bd dolt push' added to the session-close snippet

CO-TENANCY HELD ON THE LIVE FILE. Our MACHINE-STATE POLICY region survived bd's rewrite untouched, ms diff exits 0, and .claude/settings.json was not modified ('Hook already registered').

bd setup claude --check now reports CLAUDE.md as (current). ms status reports the claude harness as 'integrated'; state/tooling.json updated accordingly on the next status run.

This is the first time the two owners have written to the same live file in sequence, and it behaved exactly as the scratch experiment said it would.
close_reason: bd setup claude run; block refreshed to 970c3bf2, our region intact, ms diff clean, check reports current.

title: Decide the substantive agent operating policy for this machine
description:
Why: with machine-state-9tw.8 authoring only mechanical facts, this workstation still has no AUTHORED policy on how resident agents should behave. Today that guidance comes entirely from bd's vendor block (conservative git profile, task tracking rules, session close protocol) — text nobody here chose, inherited from an installer's default template.

That may be fine. But it should be a decision rather than an accident, and it is the user's to make, not the substrate's.

Questions, once there is appetite:
  a. Keep deferring to bd's block, or author our own operating rules in canonical/policy?
  b. If our own: which rules actually differ from bd's defaults for this machine?
  c. Does policy differ per harness, or is one neutral set correct?
  d. Shell hygiene: the rules bd ships name apt-get and brew, which are wrong here (apt-get is aliased to 'man pacman'; pacman is the real package manager, and no cp/mv/rm -i aliases exist). If we want correct guidance for this machine, it has to be ours.

Not in v0.01: the substrate must prove it can carry policy before there is any point arguing about the policy it carries.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of (a)-(d) answered, or the whole thing consciously deferred again with a reason.
- Any rules adopted land in canonical/policy fragments and reach both harnesses through the existing manifests.
notes:
ANSWERED AND APPLIED 2026-09-01.

(a) Mostly defer to bd, plus one small fragment. bd's managed block covers task tracking, the three agent profiles, and session completion, and its conservative default is what this work actually ran under. None of it restated.

(b) Four rules, in canonical/policy/20-operating.md, each one something this work actually did rather than aspiration: this repo edits a live workstation, so draft-then-apply for anything outside it; experiments run in throwaway copies, never the live tree; never issue a command that can block on a prompt; a dcg refusal is answered by narrowing the command, never by disabling the guard.

(c) One neutral set. Harness differences already live in the harness fragments. Policy that varies per harness is exactly how CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md drifted apart originally. Verified after projecting: the rules are byte-identical in both files.

(d) Fixed, and more besides. Removed 45 lines of bd-init boilerplate from AGENTS.md: the Non-Interactive Shell Commands section (recommended apt-get -y and brew, on the false premise that cp/mv/rm carry -i aliases here), the architecture blockquote citing a .beads/dolt/ path that has never existed in this workspace and which bd's own current block contradicts 60 lines below it, and a duplicate Quick Reference. Verified in a scratch copy first that bd setup codex does NOT restore any of it — that prose was written once at bd init and never maintained.

HAND-EDIT TO A FILE WE DO NOT OWN, recorded deliberately: the deletions touch bytes outside our marker pair. The rule against that constrains the PROJECTOR; a deliberate, git-tracked, one-time correction of orphaned vendor prose is a different act. It should not become precedent — if it recurs, the ownership model erodes by habit.

OPEN CONCERN: our spliced region is now 47 lines in CLAUDE.md and 46 in AGENTS.md, up from 30, and is the largest single block in either file. AGENTS.md is net 45 lines shorter overall so the files are not worse off, but the guest-in-someone-else's-file principle from machine-state-9tw.8 is stretched. If the region grows again the fix is to move the bulk into the machine-state skill, which agents load on demand, and leave a pointer in the region.
close_reason: Operating policy authored, projected to both harnesses byte-identically, and 45 lines of stale bd-init boilerplate removed from AGENTS.md.

title: Write bin/ms-agent install/uninstall helper
description:
Why: installation is the one moment the substrate reaches outside the repo. It should be a single reviewable script, reversible, and user-scope only.

What: bin/ms-agent with three subcommands:
  install   - mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user, symlink the two units from systemd/, systemctl --user daemon-reload, enable --now the timer
  uninstall - disable --now the timer, remove the two symlinks, daemon-reload
  status    - systemctl --user status for both units plus the age of state/hostwatch/latest.json

Symlinks, not copies: the repo stays the single source of truth and an edit to a unit needs only daemon-reload.

Hard rules: no sudo anywhere in the script, no writes outside ~/.config/systemd/user, idempotent (running install twice is a no-op), and it refuses to run as root.
acceptance_criteria:
- install then uninstall then install leaves the same state; no duplicate or dangling symlinks.
- Script exits non-zero with a clear message if run as root or if systemctl --user is unavailable.
- Contains no sudo, no pacman, no writes outside ~/.config/systemd/user.
- uninstall leaves the machine with no trace of the agent outside the repo.
close_reason: Superseded by machine-state-9tw: hostwatch was a new monitoring program, not the substrate beneath existing agents.
